title: Chicken Kabsa
tagline: Saudi Arabia's national dish — spiced basmati and chicken built on smoky dried lime and warm baharat.
intro: Kabsa is the beating heart of the Saudi table and the country's national dish. Basmati is cooked in a rich, tomato-based chicken broth perfumed with dried black lime (loomi), cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, then crowned with the chicken and a shower of fried nuts and raisins. Served with a fiery tomato daqoos on the side, it is the definitive dish of Saudi hospitality.

items: 1 whole chicken (about 1.2 kg), cut into 4–6 pieces
2 dried limes (loomi), pierced a few times
1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 2 bay leaves
¼ tsp turmeric or a pinch of saffron, for colour
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min and drained
3 tbsp fried almonds and pine nuts
Daqoos: 3 tomatoes blitzed with 1 garlic clove, 1 green chilli, ½ tsp cumin, simmered 10 min

method: Heat the oil and sauté the onions until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger.
Add the chicken pieces and brown lightly on all sides.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, all the spices, the pierced dried limes and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down and the oil surfaces.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked and tender, 30–40 minutes. Lift out the chicken and reserve. Strain and measure the broth (you want about 1 litre).
For colour and crispness, brush the chicken with a little oil and broil or fry until golden. Set aside.
Return the measured broth to the pot, check the salt, and stir in the saffron/turmeric. Add the drained rice.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy, 15–18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Mound the rice on a platter, arrange the chicken on top and scatter over the fried nuts, raisins and herbs. Serve with daqoos.
tips: Dried lime (loomi) is the signature Saudi flavour — pierce it so it releases its citrus-sour aroma into the broth.
Always cook the rice in the reserved broth; that is where all the flavour lives.
Broiling the chicken after boiling gives that golden, restaurant-style finish.
toServe: Serve family-style on one large platter with daqoos, salad and laban (buttermilk).
